claims.text: Data / migration: additive and reversible. No storage or backfill; the evidence gains a 'lines' key while every older key stays; switching back to CMA_RULESET=v1 on a v2-categorised statement reproduces fresh v1 categories and rule ids with no repair; P7 shows M1-M16 unchanged on every committed statement and only the listed lines change category.

claims.text: PII: per-line provenance in the evidence file carries only id, category, rule_id and reverses; payer-written descriptions do not enter evidence.

Security / authz: not applicable for a new entry point because there is none. The ruleset is chosen by the existing CMA_RULESET env var read by the existing `cma run`; no server, endpoint or command is added. Rule tables are packaged data validated on load; rule patterns are compiled regexes and descriptions are never interpolated into queries or commands. No secrets and no new dependencies (pyproject changes since 43f3e57 are only pytest marker registrations).
claims.proof_output: +markers = [contracts..., invariants..., dual_run...]  (5 added lines, no dependency change)

claims.text: Performance: categorising 10,000 lines under v2 with a profile finishes under 2 s (the categoriser part of the design's recompute target). No queries, endpoints or payloads, so N+1, indexes and pagination are not applicable.

Observability: the behaviour leaves a trace. Each evidence record names the ruleset id and sha256 plus each line's rule_id, and the evals summary names the ruleset. The design says there is no remote alerting; instead the tool refuses (RulesetError) on an unknown or malformed table.
claims.proof_output: record['ruleset'] == {'id': 'v2', 'sha256': ...} and every line's (category, rule_id) asserted: PASSED

claims.text: Operability: behind a flag (CMA_RULESET; default stays v1) and rollback is exercised in tests (v1 after v2, cma run under v1). Config change for deploy: CMA_RULESET=v2 to opt in; no secrets.

Review finding regressions, generalised: every pot/savings word plus RENT/PAYROLL/BANK CHARGES is an own-account transfer; every refund word plus generic FINANCE/LOAN is refund_in; Post Office/PayPoint names alone (bare, BACS, FPS) stay OTHER; every cash phrase behind any electronic-rail prefix is never cash_deposit. New test added.

Docs: README documents v2's lists, the precedence, the per-line rule ids in the evidence, and CMA_RULESET=v1 as the rollback; the categorise.py module docstring states the precedence and the rule_id formats. The design decision is already recorded in design.md (Sub-decision: where the categorisation rules live).
claims.proof_output: README hunk shows 'CMA_RULESET=v2 cma run ...' and '... CMA_RULESET=v1 is the rollback.'

dispositions.finding: major: The rent rule wins over an explicit transfer to an applicant's own pot (src/cma/rules/v2.yaml:128)
dispositions.evidence: classify('TFR TO POT RENT', -300) -> (own_account_transfer, 'v2:own_pots_savings'). own_pots_savings is now the first unprotected rule, ahead of rent, payroll and bank_fees. test_overlaps_from_the_review_hold_for_every_listed_word passes for every pot word with every purpose.

dispositions.finding: major: Generic finance wording takes precedence over an explicit refund and records debt the applicant did not draw (src/cma/rules/v2.yaml:110)
dispositions.evidence: classify('CARD REFUND ACME RETAIL FINANCE', 75) -> (refund_in, 'v2:refunds'); 'LOAN REFUND' and 'FINANCE REFUND' -> refund_in. The loan_drawdown rule now has `unless` with the refund words. A named lender still wins (IWOCA REFUND -> lender_drawdown, R21). The generalised test passes for every refund word.

dispositions.finding: major: The Post Office name alone is enough to turn an electronic transfer into a cash deposit and inflate trading receipts (src/cma/rules/v2.yaml:172)
dispositions.evidence: classify('BACS CREDIT POST OFFICE LTD', 500) and 'POST OFFICE COUNTERS', 'POST OFFICE', 'PAYPOINT' -> (other, 'v2:default'); 'FPS CREDIT POST OFFICE CASH' -> other. test_cma_run_under_v2_keeps_a_post_office_transfer_out_of_trading_receipts passes, with M2 = 4*2000 and the line not in M2's evidence.

notes: Gaps for the owner (no code change, as the scope is design-level): (1) Electronic-rail detection for cash relies on a prefix anchored at the start of the description (FPS/BACS/CHAPS/TFR/TRANSFER/SO/STO); a bank whose export puts the rail later (e.g. 'CREDIT FPS ...') or uses another word would let payer-typed cash wording through. Each bank-CSV importer profile should confirm its rail wording. (2) 'RENT POT' with no move wording (no TO/FROM POT, POT TRANSFER) still goes to rent; if pot names appear like this in real Monzo exports, add the export's own wording to own_pots_savings. (3) own_pots_savings matches SAVINGS in either direction, so 'INTEREST ON SAVINGS' lands in own-account transfers (M19) rather than other explained (M24). Both are non-trading, so M2/M9/M16 do not move, but the bucket split does; the owner should decide whether interest should win. (4) No CHANGELOG file exists in the repo; the README is the only user-facing note, so a release-note line would need a home first. (5) The design has no remote alerting by design; the failure signal is refusal (RulesetError), so 'alert' and 'runbook' checklist lines are met only by that refusal and the README. (6) ruff over the whole repo reports 14 errors, all in .bridgie/runs/** helper scripts from earlier runs, not in src/tests/evals.
